items.title: Clem Raymond Interview, 1958-08-25
items.q: Mr. Humphrey was different I was just across the street from him... he wouldn't charge me nothing

ctx.x: oh yeah we'll talk about that later when we get it out here yeah but I'd still like to hear more a little bit more about your lessons with the about T.O. what kind of a teacher was he was he real strict or did he did he another thing did he ever play with you did he ever have his clarinet there or did he just

oh yeah he used his clarinet because he showed me how to make different passages and then he would play something and say well boy you do this way you do that way and so on well I wasn't that far advanced and if I didn't go I had to pay the 25 cents for the lesson just to see charge 25 cents a lesson well that was a lot of money that's right yeah there's a day she got her quarters where you go well that's that's what I paid 25 cents a lesson and by moving around and working all the time you want to cut it no…
yeah where did he live about? I never did know
